title: [finding] the 429 details fences in error-handling.mdx teach three members no producer emits, and omit the one it does
body:
Found while fixing #15855, which corrects one member of these same JSON fences. That card's fence is deliberately narrow — "only the `details` members named `retry_after`" — so the rest of the bag is filed here rather than swept in.

Measured on `origin/main` at `9a89a0040`; line numbers are from that tree and are **pre-#15855**, which only renames `retry_after` in place.

## The producer emits exactly two members

Both 429 emitters build the same `details` bag, and nothing else:

- `packages/runtime/src/endpoint-policy.ts:356` — `details: { retryAfterSeconds: retryAfterSec, resetAt: new Date(decision.resetAt).toISOString() }`
- `packages/runtime/src/security/inbound-rate-limit.ts:359` — byte-identical bag, the server-level 429

Pinned by `packages/runtime/src/endpoint-policy.test.ts:181` and `packages/runtime/src/dispatcher-plugin.endpoint-fallback.integration.test.ts:513`.

## The docs teach five, three of which no producer emits

`content/docs/protocol/kernel/error-handling.mdx:423` and `:655` both teach:

| documented member | emitted by any producer? |
|:--|:--|
| `retry_after` | no — the producer spells it `retryAfterSeconds`; **this one is #15855 and is being fixed there** |
| `limit` | no |
| `window` | no |
| `quota_reset` | no — the producer emits `resetAt`, which is the same fact under a different name |
| `upgrade_url` (`:655` only) | no |

The evidence for every "no" row is the producer itself, not a word search: both emitter lines are **exhaustive object literals** with exactly two members, so anything else the page names is not in the bag. Two supplementary readings, each with a positive control on the same corpus so a zero is a reading:

- `quota_reset` anywhere in `packages/**`: **0 hits**.
- `upgrade_url` anywhere in `packages/**`: **1 hit**, and it is not an emitter — `packages/cloud-connection/src/runtime-config-plugin.ts:42`, a prose comment about the control plane's own `upgrade_url` dialect.
- Positive control on the same corpus: `resetAt` returns 19 hits in `packages/**`, including both producer lines above.

`resetAt` is the interesting one: the fact is emitted, under a name the page never mentions, so a client copying this fence loses a value the server actually sends **and** reads three that were never there.

## Same failure direction as #15855, one notch quieter

A client written from these fences reads `details.quota_reset` and gets `undefined` on every real 429 — no error, just a missing field. It does not cause the retry-storm #15855 describes (that one is specific to the backoff member), which is why this is filed separately rather than raised to that card's priority. But it is the same class: a JSON fence a client is meant to copy, where copying it fails.

## Why nothing catches it

Carried over from #15855's triage and re-checked here: `details` is `z.unknown()` on the ADR-0112 envelope, so no schema constrains its members, and no gate compares a documented `details` key against what any producer emits. These are JSON fences rather than TypeScript, so the type-check does not reach them either. After #15855 lands, this page's backoff member will be correct and the rest of the bag will still be unbacked and still ungated.

## Suggested fix

Reduce both fences to what the producer emits (`retryAfterSeconds`, `resetAt`), or keep the illustrative members and mark the section as illustrative rather than as the wire shape. The 503 fence at `:531` deserves the same question — it carries `reason`, `retry_after` and `estimated_completion`, and no 503 producer on this tree emits a `details` bag at all.

Related: #15855.
